To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) HSP70 is expressed in the kidney of rats with salt-sensitive hypertension and is the target of an antigen-specific immune response; 2) HSP70 gene transfer to the renal vein induces a rise in blood pressure and hypertension in rats sensitized to this antigen; 3) HSP70 induces a strong proliferate response in peripheral lymphocytes of patients and controls with essential hypertension; 4) Immune tolerance to HSP70 is associated with protection from hypertension and renal injury
(1) HSP70, a protein overexpressed in hypertension, induces a T cell clonal response in the kidney that contributes to salt-sensitive hypertension.
immune reactivity to HSP70 expressed by the kidney is a cause of salt-sensitive and essential hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the immune response in salt-sensitive hypertension.
the role of the immune system in the development of salt sensitive hypertension.
the identification of the mechanisms of immune reactivity in hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the immune system plays a role in the pathogenesis of hypertension and that the immune response in the kidneys of salt-sensitive hypertensive rats is driven by a specific antigen (HSP70), and this response can be blocked by immune tolerance to HSP70.
HSP70 is a key antigen that is involved in salt-sensitive hypertension.
immune reactivity to HSP70 expressed by the kidney is cause and effect of salt-sensitive hypertension and that immune tolerance to this antigen prevents the development of the condition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
immune reactivity to a stress protein expressed in the kidney, HSP70, is a cause of salt-sensitive essential hypertension.
the immune system plays a role in the development of salt sensitive hypertension.
the immune response to HSP70 expressed by the kidney is cause for salt-sensitive hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
salt sensitive hypertension is an autoimmune disease that is driven by the immune response to heat shock proteins in the kidney.
immune cells are not bystanders but active participants in the pathophysiology of salt-sensitive hypertension.
hypertension is not just a disease of the blood vessels, but it is an autoimmune disease.
